stops.name: White Pebble Suites Milos
stops.description: A sleek stone-and-plaster villa-style property with private plunge pools and sweeping views over the bay — the perfect Milos base.

stops.name: Sarakiniko Beach
stops.description: Milos' iconic 'moon beach' — sculpted white volcanic rock meeting vivid turquoise water, unlike anywhere else in Greece.
stops.tip: Go early morning to beat the crowds and get the best light.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended from accommodation.

stops.name: Tsigrado Beach
stops.description: A hidden gem of a cove accessible only via a rope-and-ladder climb down the cliff face, rewarding visitors with seclusion and clear water.
stops.tip: Be ready for the ladder climb down — not far from Sarakiniko.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Sarakiniko.

stops.name: O Hamos Restaurant
stops.description: A beloved local taverna serving traditional Greek grills on terracotta plates with a handwritten menu that adds to its charm.
stops.tip: 10/10, so worth the hype — the handwritten menu makes it even better.

stops.name: Papafragkas Beach
stops.description: A small, private sea-cave cove reachable by a short climb down, offering sheltered swimming surrounded by dramatic white cliffs.
stops.tip: Small and private — worth the short climb down.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from lunch spot.

stops.name: Utopia Café, Plaka
stops.description: A hilltop café-bar in the village of Plaka with unreal panoramic sunset views over the Aegean.
stops.tip: Best spot on the island for sunset drinks — views are unreal.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive up to Plaka village.

days.label: Kleftiko Full-Day Boat Trip & Astakas Dinner

stops.name: Kleftiko Sea Caves Boat Trip
stops.description: A full-day boat trip to Milos' most spectacular sea caves and pirate coves, with some of the clearest water in the Aegean — a non-negotiable highlight of the island.
stops.tip: Book a full-day trip in advance — you can't come to Milos and skip this.
stops.transfer_note: Boat departs from Adamas port.

stops.name: Astakas Restaurant
stops.description: A well-regarded local seafood and Greek cuisine restaurant recommended for dinner after the boat day.

stops.name: Fyropotamos Village
stops.description: One of Milos' most beautiful and authentic little fishing villages, with colourful syrmata boathouses built into the rock and crystal-clear water perfect for swimming.
stops.tip: You'll feel like a local here — great morning swim spot.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended.

stops.name: Mandrakia Village
stops.description: A charming syrmata fishing village with traditional blue-and-white boathouses and a lively waterfront swim spot.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Fyropotamos.

stops.name: Medusa Restaurant, Mandrakia
stops.description: A waterfront taverna in Mandrakia village serving lunch right on the water's edge.
stops.tip: Right on the water — great spot for a long lunch.
stops.transfer_note: Walking distance within Mandrakia village.

stops.name: Fyriplaka Beach
stops.description: Widely considered one of the most beautiful beaches on Milos, with golden sand, white cliffs, and vivid turquoise water.
stops.tip: Easily one of the prettiest beaches on the island — save it for the afternoon.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended from Mandrakia.

stops.name: Plaka Village
stops.description: The hilltop capital of Milos with whitewashed Cycladic architecture, great restaurants, and the best sunset viewpoints on the island.
stops.tip: End the day here with dinner after the beach.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive up from Fyriplaka.

stops.name: Mytakas Beach
stops.description: A quiet, less-visited beach on the northern coast of Milos with calm, clear water.
stops.tip: Pack snacks and water for a full beach-hopping day.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended.

stops.name: Alogomandra Beach
stops.description: A secluded turquoise cove with dramatic white rock backdrops, one of Milos' hidden beauties.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Mytakas.

stops.name: Kolympisionas Beach
stops.description: A remote and unspoilt beach on the island's south coast, worth the drive for its seclusion and stunning scenery.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended.

stops.name: O Hamos Restaurant
stops.description: Back to this beloved local taverna for a repeat lunch — the creator says it's honestly that good.
stops.tip: Stop back here for lunch — it's honestly that good.

stops.name: White Pebble Suites Milos
stops.description: Finish the trip with a farewell dinner at the on-site restaurant of this beautiful suites property, rounding off four perfect days in Milos.
stops.tip: Perfect spot to end your last evening in Milos.
stops.transfer_note: At your accommodation.

routes.summary: Milos is one of Greece's most stunning volcanic islands, famous for its otherworldly white rock formations, impossibly clear turquoise water, and colourful fishing villages. This itinerary covers the island's greatest hits — from the lunar landscape of Sarakiniko to the sea caves of Kleftiko — with a mix of beach-hopping, local taverna lunches, and sunset drinks in hilltop Plaka.
routes.car_rental_note: The video explicitly states you'll need a car to get around, as beaches and villages are spread across the island.

stops.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
stops.description: Mexico City's iconic art nouveau and art deco palace, home to world-class murals and performing arts.

stops.name: Palacio Postal (Correo Mayor)
stops.description: A stunning Porfirian-era postal palace with ornate golden ironwork staircases inside.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Bellas Artes

stops.name: Ángel de la Independencia
stops.description: Mexico City's most beloved monument, a golden winged victory column on the grand Paseo de la Reforma.
stops.transfer_note: Short taxi or metro ride from the Historic Center

stops.name: Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul)
stops.description: The vibrant blue house where Frida Kahlo was born and lived, now a fascinating museum dedicated to her life and art.

stops.name: Mercado Artesanal Mexicano, Coyoacán
stops.description: A colorful public market in Coyoacán perfect for picking up crafts and local snacks.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Coyoacán

stops.name: Xochimilco Canals
stops.description: Cruise the ancient Aztec waterways on a festive trajinera boat surrounded by floating gardens and mariachi music.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive or uber south from Coyoacán

stops.name: Teotihuacán Archaeological Zone
stops.description: One of the greatest pre-Columbian cities in the Americas, home to the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon along the Avenue of the Dead.
stops.tip: Take a hot air balloon ride over the pyramids at sunrise for an unforgettable perspective.
stops.transfer_note: Early morning tour departs Mexico City before sunrise

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
stops.description: Mexico's most sacred Catholic site and one of the most-visited pilgrimage destinations in the world.
stops.transfer_note: Return drive from Teotihuacán passes near the Basilica on the way back to the city

stops.name: Great Pyramid of Cholula (Zona Arqueológica de Cholula)
stops.description: The world's largest pyramid by volume, topped by a Spanish colonial church and offering sweeping views of Popocatépetl.
stops.transfer_note: Roughly 2-hour drive from Mexico City

stops.name: Puebla Historic Center
stops.description: A UNESCO-listed colonial city famous for its ornate Baroque architecture, Talavera tiles, and mole poblano cuisine.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Cholula

stops.name: Grutas de Tolantongo
stops.description: A breathtaking canyon in Hidalgo state with turquoise thermal river pools, natural cave pools, and dramatic waterfalls carved into the mountainside.
stops.tip: Book accommodation in advance as day tours make it a very long day from Mexico City.
stops.transfer_note: Long drive north of Mexico City, guided tour recommended

stops.name: Cuernavaca
stops.description: The 'City of Eternal Spring,' known for its pleasant climate, colonial palaces, and the Cathedral of the Assumption.
stops.transfer_note: About 1.5-hour drive south of Mexico City

stops.name: Taxco
stops.description: A perfectly preserved colonial silver-mining town with cobblestone streets, a stunning pink baroque cathedral, and narrow hillside alleys.
stops.transfer_note: About 1.5-hour drive south of Cuernavaca

days.label: Flight to San Cristóbal de las Casas

stops.name: San Cristóbal de las Casas
stops.description: A highland colonial gem in Chiapas with vibrantly painted streets, indigenous markets, and a rich Tzotzil Maya cultural scene.
stops.tip: Fly via Tuxtla Gutiérrez airport and transfer up to San Cristóbal by road.
stops.transfer_note: Flight from Mexico City to Tuxtla, then approx. 1-hour drive up to San Cristóbal

stops.name: Cascadas de Agua Azul
stops.description: A series of stunning turquoise cascading waterfalls in the Chiapas jungle, perfect for swimming.
stops.transfer_note: Long day tour drive from San Cristóbal

stops.name: Cascada de Misol-Ha
stops.description: A spectacular 35-metre jungle waterfall with a cave you can walk behind for a dramatic viewpoint.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Agua Azul en route to Palenque

stops.name: Palenque Archaeological Zone
stops.description: One of the most impressive Maya archaeological sites, with soaring jungle-clad temples including the iconic Temple of the Inscriptions.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Misol-Ha

stops.name: San Juan Chamula
stops.description: An indigenous Tzotzil village near San Cristóbal with a fascinating syncretic church where candles, incense, and shamanic rituals replace pews.
stops.tip: Photography is strictly forbidden inside the church — respect local customs.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive or tour from San Cristóbal

stops.name: Zinacantán
stops.description: A Tzotzil weaving village known for its intricate flower-patterned textiles and a beautifully decorated local church.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Chamula

stops.name: Cañón del Sumidero
stops.description: A dramatic 1,000-metre-deep canyon on the Grijalva River, best explored by boat past towering cliffs, crocodiles, and waterfalls.
stops.transfer_note: Day tour by road from San Cristóbal, about 1.5 hours

stops.name: Chiapa de Corzo
stops.description: A charming riverside colonial town at the mouth of the Sumidero Canyon, known for its large colonial fountain and vibrant local culture.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive or boat access from the canyon entrance

stops.name: Cancún Beach
stops.description: The dazzling white-sand Caribbean beach of Cancún with warm turquoise waters, perfect for unwinding after days of touring.
stops.tip: Spend the afternoon relaxing after your flight from Tuxtla.
stops.transfer_note: Flight from Tuxtla Gutiérrez to Cancún, then hotel zone beach

stops.name: Chichén Itzá
stops.description: One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, this magnificent Maya city features the iconic El Castillo pyramid and the Great Ball Court.
stops.tip: Arrive as early as possible to beat the crowds and the heat.
stops.transfer_note: About 2.5-hour drive west from Cancún

stops.name: Cenote Ik Kil
stops.description: A spectacular open-air cenote near Chichén Itzá with vines cascading down the walls into a deep turquoise pool.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Chichén Itzá

stops.name: Valladolid
stops.description: A charming Yucatán colonial city with a colorful main square and the stunning underground Cenote Suytun nearby.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Cenote Ik Kil

stops.name: Cenote Suytun
stops.description: A magical underground cenote in Valladolid with a stone walkway leading to a sunlit pool, perfect for swimming and photos.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Valladolid town center

stops.name: Río Lagartos Biosphere Reserve
stops.description: A pristine coastal biosphere on the northern Yucatán coast where boat tours bring you up close to wild flamingo flocks.
stops.transfer_note: Long drive north from Cancún, full-day tour recommended

stops.name: Las Coloradas (Lagunas Coloradas)
stops.description: Striking bubblegum-pink lagoons created by micro-organisms in the salt flats, one of Yucatán's most photogenic natural wonders.
stops.tip: Visit in the morning for the best pink colour intensity.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Río Lagartos

stops.name: Cenote Canamayte
stops.description: A scenic jungle cenote near Tulum with blue morpho butterflies and crystal-clear waters ideal for snorkelling.
stops.transfer_note: About 1.5-hour drive south of Cancún

stops.name: Akumal Bay
stops.description: A sheltered bay famous for snorkelling directly with wild sea turtles in their natural habitat.
stops.tip: Arrive early before tour groups arrive for the best turtle encounters.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Cenote Canamayte

stops.name: Tulum Archaeological Zone
stops.description: Dramatic clifftop Maya ruins overlooking a turquoise Caribbean bay, one of Mexico's most photogenic ancient sites.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive south from Akumal

days.label: Last Morning on the Beach & Departure

stops.name: Cancún Hotel Zone Beach
stops.description: Cancún's iconic Caribbean beach with powdery white sand and impossibly clear turquoise water — the perfect send-off before your flight.
stops.tip: Chill here before your return flight home.

routes.summary: Mexico is a country of staggering contrasts, from ancient pyramids and colonial palaces to jungle waterfalls, indigenous villages, and Caribbean beaches. This two-week route sweeps from Mexico City through Chiapas and down to the Yucatán Peninsula, combining major archaeological sites, dramatic natural landscapes, and colorful colonial towns. It's an ambitious, culture-rich adventure that rewards curious travelers willing to cover serious ground.

stops.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City
stops.description: The historic heart of Mexico City, packed with grand colonial architecture, bustling plazas, and centuries of culture.

stops.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
stops.description: Mexico City's iconic art nouveau and art deco palace, home to stunning murals and a gilded dome visible from across the city.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Centro Histórico

stops.name: Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución)
stops.description: One of the largest city squares in the world and the political and cultural epicentre of Mexico City.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Palacio de Bellas Artes

stops.name: Palacio Postal (Correo Mayor)
stops.description: A breathtaking Baroque-Plateresque post office building from 1907 with ornate ironwork interiors worth exploring.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Zócalo

stops.name: Café Giglo (rooftop view of Bellas Artes)
stops.description: A rooftop café offering one of the best views over Palacio de Bellas Artes with colourful iced drinks.
stops.transfer_note: Within Centro Histórico

stops.name: Castillo de Chapultepec
stops.description: A hilltop castle set within a vast urban forest, filled with opulent stained-glass galleries and panoramic city views.
stops.transfer_note: Metro or taxi to Chapultepec Park

stops.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
stops.description: One of the world's great museums, showcasing Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilisations including the famous Aztec Sun Stone.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Chapultepec Castle within the park

stops.name: Teotihuacán Archaeological Zone
stops.description: An awe-inspiring ancient city featuring the massive Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, best explored early in the morning.
stops.tip: Visit pyramids of the Sun and the Moon
stops.transfer_note: Bus or organised tour from Mexico City, roughly one hour away

stops.name: Hot Air Balloon Ride over Teotihuacán
stops.description: A sunrise hot air balloon flight over the pyramids offers a spectacular bird's-eye perspective of the ancient ruins.
stops.tip: Book at sunrise for the best experience
stops.transfer_note: Departs from the Teotihuacán site at dawn

stops.name: Panadería Rosetta
stops.description: A celebrated artisan bakery in Roma Norte known for its guava-filled pastries and European-quality breads.
stops.transfer_note: Metro or short taxi from Centro

stops.name: Roma Norte neighbourhood
stops.description: A tree-lined, art nouveau neighbourhood filled with independent cafés, vintage shops, and beautiful architecture.
stops.transfer_note: Walkable from Panadería Rosetta

stops.name: Condesa neighbourhood
stops.description: An adjacent leafy district with art deco buildings, local parks, and a relaxed café culture beloved by locals.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Roma Norte

stops.name: Nima Urban Spa
stops.description: A stylish urban spa tucked behind greenery in Roma Norte, offering a tranquil wellness retreat in the city.
stops.transfer_note: Within Roma Norte neighbourhood

stops.name: Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul)
stops.description: The iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived with Diego Rivera, now a deeply personal museum filled with her art and belongings.
stops.tip: Book tickets well in advance — they sell out fast
stops.transfer_note: Metro or taxi to Coyoacán

stops.name: Centro de Coyoacán
stops.description: A charming, cobblestoned historic village within the city with colonial churches, artisan markets, and lively plazas.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from La Casa Azul

stops.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
stops.description: A final stroll past Mexico City's most iconic building before heading home.

routes.summary: Mexico City is one of Latin America's most vibrant capitals, blending ancient history, world-class museums, and a thriving food scene across its colourful neighbourhoods. This first-timer itinerary covers the grand Centro Histórico, the leafy parklands of Chapultepec, a day trip to the pyramids of Teotihuacán, and the bohemian streets of Roma Norte, Condesa, and Coyoacán.

stops.name: Budva Old Town
stops.description: A compact Venetian-era walled town with atmospheric stone alleys, flower-draped cafés, and a stunning Adriatic backdrop.

stops.name: Budva Beach
stops.description: The main sandy beach beside the Old Town, with thatched sunshade umbrellas and golden sunset views toward St. Nicholas Island.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Old Town

stops.name: Lustica Peninsula
stops.description: A rugged, largely undeveloped peninsula jutting into the Bay of Kotor, with crystal-clear coves, hidden beaches, and laid-back fishing harbours.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended from Budva

stops.name: Marina Village LUSTICA Bay
stops.description: A second day to explore the quieter bays and rocky swimming spots on the Lustica Peninsula's southern tip.

stops.name: Sveti Stefan
stops.description: Montenegro's most iconic sight — a 15th-century fortified island village connected to the mainland by a narrow causeway, surrounded by pink-pebble beaches and turquoise water.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive north from Lustica Peninsula

stops.name: Sveti Stefan Beach
stops.description: The public beach flanking the island causeway offers some of the most photogenic swimming in the Adriatic.
stops.transfer_note: Directly beside Sveti Stefan island

stops.name: Kotor Old Town
stops.description: A UNESCO-listed medieval walled city nestled between steep karst mountains and the Bay of Kotor, filled with Romanesque churches, piazzas, and cobbled lanes.
stops.transfer_note: Drive north along the Bay of Kotor from Sveti Stefan

days.label: Perast & Our Lady of the Rocks

stops.name: Perast
stops.description: A beautifully preserved Baroque village strung along the bay shore, with elegant palaces and sweeping views to its two famous islets.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Kotor along the bay

stops.name: Our Lady of the Rocks, Perast
stops.description: A 17th-century island church built on an artificial reef, reached by a short boat taxi from Perast, housing a remarkable collection of ex-votos and Flemish paintings.
stops.transfer_note: Short boat taxi from Perast waterfront

stops.name: Bay of Kotor
stops.description: The spectacular fjord-like bay offers a final scenic drive past historic villages and dramatic mountain reflections on the water.

routes.summary: Montenegro packs an extraordinary range of scenery into a small country — dramatic Adriatic coastline, medieval walled towns, and mountain backdrops all within easy reach of each other. This 7-day itinerary sweeps from the beaches and old town of Budva down to the wild Lustica Peninsula, then up through the iconic island of Sveti Stefan and the Bay of Kotor's jewels, Kotor and Perast.

stops.name: Waikiki Resort Hotel
stops.description: Waikiki is the beating heart of Hawaiian tourism, putting you steps from the beach, restaurants, and Kalākaua Avenue's buzzing nightlife.
stops.tip: Keep it light on arrival — jet lag is real.
stops.transfer_note: Direct from Honolulu International Airport, roughly 30 min by car or shuttle.

stops.name: Waikiki Beach
stops.description: Oahu's iconic crescent of white sand backed by the Diamond Head crater, perfect for a relaxed first swim in the Pacific.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from any Waikiki hotel.

stops.name: Kalākaua Avenue, Waikiki
stops.description: Waikiki's famous beachfront boulevard lined with restaurants, open-air shops, and street performers — ideal for a gentle sunset stroll and dinner.
stops.transfer_note: Runs directly along the beachfront in Waikiki.

stops.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
stops.description: A deeply moving WWII landmark where you can visit the USS Arizona Memorial and learn about the 1941 attack that changed history.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended from Waikiki, roughly 30–40 min drive west.

stops.name: Diamond Head State Monument
stops.description: Oahu's most iconic volcanic crater offers a rewarding hike with panoramic views over Waikiki and the Pacific from the summit ridge.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive east from Waikiki.

stops.name: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
stops.description: A stunning protected marine bay renowned for exceptionally clear water and abundant tropical fish, making it one of Hawaii's top snorkeling spots.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive east along the coast from Diamond Head.

stops.name: North Shore, Oahu
stops.description: A legendary stretch of Oahu's northern coastline famous for enormous winter swells, laid-back surf culture, and natural beauty.
stops.tip: Drive up from Waikiki — car is essential for this day.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended from Waikiki, roughly 1 hour drive north.

stops.name: Laniakea Beach (Turtle Beach)
stops.description: Famous for Hawaiian green sea turtles that come ashore to bask on the sand, making for unforgettable wildlife encounters.
stops.transfer_note: Along the Kamehameha Highway on the North Shore.

stops.name: Banzai Pipeline
stops.description: One of the world's most famous surf breaks, where you can watch elite surfers tackle massive, hollow waves in a spectacular natural arena.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Laniakea Beach along the North Shore.

stops.name: North Shore garlic shrimp food trucks
stops.description: A beloved local institution — roadside shrimp trucks serving buttery, garlic-drenched shrimp plates that are a quintessential North Shore experience.
stops.tip: Try garlic shrimp from local food trucks.
stops.transfer_note: Clustered along the North Shore highway near Haleiwa.

stops.name: Kahului Airport, Maui
stops.description: Short inter-island flight from Honolulu to Maui, the 'Valley Isle', marking the start of a more adventurous chapter of the trip.
stops.tip: Book a morning flight to maximise beach time on arrival.
stops.transfer_note: Short inter-island flight from Honolulu.

stops.name: Grand Wailea, A Waldorf Astoria Resort
stops.description: Both Kaanapali and Wailea are Maui's premier resort areas, offering beachfront accommodation, world-class dining, and easy access to the island's best beaches.
stops.transfer_note: Car recommended from Kahului Airport, roughly 30–45 min drive.

stops.name: Kaanapali Beach
stops.description: A gorgeous three-mile stretch of golden sand on Maui's west coast, backed by luxury resorts and offering calm, swimmable water and brilliant sunsets.
stops.tip: Optional: watch the sunset from the beach.
stops.transfer_note: Steps from Kaanapali resort hotels.

stops.name: Road to Hana, Maui
stops.description: One of the world's great scenic drives — a winding 64-mile highway through rainforest, past waterfalls, sea cliffs, and remote Hawaiian villages.
stops.tip: This is a full-day adventure — start early!
stops.transfer_note: Car essential; depart your Maui hotel very early morning.

stops.name: Twin Falls, Maui
stops.description: An easily accessible pair of stunning waterfalls near the start of the Road to Hana, surrounded by lush tropical jungle.
stops.tip: One of the first stops on the Road to Hana — don't skip it.
stops.transfer_note: Early stop along the Road to Hana, roughly 2 miles past Haiku.

stops.name: Wai'anapanapa State Park
stops.description: Maui's dramatic black sand beach formed by volcanic rock, with sea caves, blowholes, and a striking contrast of dark sand against turquoise water.
stops.tip: Advance reservations required to enter the park.
stops.transfer_note: Near the end of the Road to Hana drive.

stops.name: Haleakalā National Park
stops.description: Maui's dormant volcanic crater summit at 10,000 ft offers a otherworldly landscape and one of the most spectacular sunrises on earth.
stops.tip: Book your sunrise parking reservation well in advance.
stops.transfer_note: Car essential; depart your hotel before 3am to reach the summit for sunrise.

stops.name: Molokini Crater
stops.description: A partially submerged volcanic crater just off Maui's southwest coast, forming a marine sanctuary with exceptional visibility and diverse marine life.
stops.tip: Book a snorkeling tour boat in advance.
stops.transfer_note: Boat tour departs from Maalaea Harbor, roughly 30 min drive from Wailea.

stops.name: Luau experience, Maui
stops.description: An evening of traditional Hawaiian food, music, and hula dancing — a festive and culturally rich way to spend the final full night in Maui.
stops.tip: No specific place — pick any similar option nearby.
stops.transfer_note: Various locations across Maui; check your resort for recommendations.

stops.name: Kaanapali Beach (final morning)
stops.description: One last leisurely morning on Maui's finest beach before heading to the airport — a perfect, relaxed send-off from the islands.
stops.transfer_note: Steps from your Kaanapali or Wailea hotel.

stops.name: Whale watching tour, Maui
stops.description: Seasonal boat excursion (December–April) to spot humpback whales in the warm waters of the Auau Channel — a bucket-list wildlife experience.
stops.tip: Seasonal only: December to April.
stops.transfer_note: Boats depart from Lahaina or Maalaea Harbor.

routes.summary: Hawaii offers an irresistible mix of volcanic landscapes, world-class surf, turquoise waters, and rich Polynesian culture spread across its stunning islands. This explorer-focused itinerary splits the week between Oahu — covering Waikiki, Pearl Harbor, Diamond Head, Hanauma Bay, and the North Shore — before island-hopping to Maui for the Road to Hana, a Haleakalā sunrise, snorkeling at Molokini Crater, and a traditional luau.

stops.name: Guesthouse Step
stops.description: A casual guesthouse-style stay with bikes available to hire and direct access to the bay waterfront path.
stops.tip: Bikes available on-site — great for riding the red cycle path along the bay.

stops.name: Bay of Kotor waterfront promenade, Kotor
stops.description: A scenic walk or bike ride along the bright-red cycle path hugging the edge of the bay with mountain views.
stops.tip: Grab a SUP board or hire bikes and ride along the waterfront.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or bike ride from accommodation

stops.name: Beach on the Bay of Kotor
stops.description: A small pebbly bay beach right on the waterfront with turquoise water and mountain backdrops.
stops.tip: About a 40 minute walk from the Old Town.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk along waterfront path

stops.name: Kotor Old Town
stops.description: A UNESCO-listed medieval walled city with honey-coloured stone buildings, vibrant squares, and atmospheric narrow lanes.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or drive from bay accommodation

stops.name: BBQ Tanja, Kotor
stops.description: A beloved local BBQ spot known for its grilled meats, with staff in branded uniforms — a must-visit for carnivores.
stops.tip: Go around 5 PM to beat the crowds.
stops.transfer_note: Within or near Kotor Old Town

stops.name: Cathedral Pasta Bar, Kotor Old Town
stops.description: A well-loved pasta restaurant set within the Old Town's stone walls serving rich, generous portions.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within the Old Town

stops.name: Kraken Wine Bar, Kotor
stops.description: A waterside wine bar with stunning bay views, recommended for its wine and bruschetta-style small plates.
stops.tip: Make a reservation in advance — it books out.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Old Town

stops.name: Ladder of Kotor (Serpentine hiking trail)
stops.description: A dramatic zigzag hiking trail carved into the cliff above Kotor offering breathtaking panoramas over the Bay of Kotor.
stops.tip: Takes about 40 minutes round trip from the Old Town walls.
stops.transfer_note: Starts at the walls of Kotor Old Town

stops.name: Kotor Fortress (Castle of San Giovanni)
stops.description: The iconic hilltop fortress above Kotor reachable via the ancient stone walls, with sweeping views over the old town and bay.
stops.transfer_note: Accessed via the Old Town walls stairway

stops.name: Forza KUK, Kotor
stops.description: A dramatic open-air restaurant and bar perched on a clifftop above the bay, perfect for sunset dining with panoramic views.
stops.transfer_note: Above the Old Town — car or taxi recommended

stops.name: Kotor Cable Car
stops.description: A scenic cable car ride ascending the steep mountain above Kotor, offering jaw-dropping aerial views of the bay and old town below.
stops.tip: Book tickets in advance online.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Old Town to cable car base station

stops.name: Monte 1350 Bar, Kotor
stops.description: A stylish mountaintop bar at 1,350 metres with live DJs, violin performances, and sweeping views over the mountains — ideal for sunset drinks.
stops.tip: Go to Monty 1350 for the sunset — pay extra for the fast cable car.
stops.transfer_note: At the top of the Kotor cable car

routes.summary: Kotor is a stunningly preserved medieval walled city nestled between dramatic karst mountains and the glittering Bay of Kotor, offering a rare blend of history, adventure, and Adriatic beauty. This route covers the Old Town's cobbled streets and waterfront dining, active pursuits like hiking the Ladder of Kotor and riding the cable car, and unforgettable sunset experiences at mountaintop bars above the bay.

stops.name: Meiji Shrine
stops.description: A serene Shinto shrine set within a vast forested park in the heart of the city, a tranquil contrast to the urban buzz outside.
stops.tip: Go early morning to avoid crowds and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or subway from Harajuku station.

stops.name: Takeshita Street
stops.description: Harajuku's famous pedestrian lane packed with quirky fashion boutiques, crepe stalls, and youth subculture at its most colourful.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Meiji Shrine.

stops.name: Plaza Harakado & Plaza Omokado
stops.description: Two adjacent fashion and lifestyle complexes in Harajuku showcasing Japanese streetwear, design brands, and contemporary culture.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Takeshita Street.

stops.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
stops.description: One of Tokyo's largest and most beautiful parks, perfect for a relaxed stroll among manicured Japanese, French, and English gardens.
stops.transfer_note: Short subway ride or walk from Harajuku.

stops.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
stops.description: Twin-towered civic landmark in Shinjuku with free observation decks offering sweeping panoramic views of the city and Mount Fuji on clear days.
stops.tip: Free entry to the observation deck — great budget alternative to paid towers.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Shinjuku.

stops.name: Omoide Yokocho & Kabukicho
stops.description: Omoide Yokocho is a narrow, smoky alley of tiny yakitori bars, while Kabukicho is Tokyo's neon-drenched entertainment and nightlife district next door.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Shinjuku.

stops.name: Godzilla Head, Shinjuku
stops.description: A giant Godzilla head emerging from the rooftop of the Toho Cinema building, a beloved pop-culture landmark and photo stop in Kabukicho.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Kabukicho.

stops.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai
stops.description: A labyrinth of around 200 tiny atmospheric bars, each seating only a handful of guests, perfect for a unique late-night Tokyo drinking experience.
stops.tip: Some bars charge a small cover fee — check before you sit down.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Shinjuku.

stops.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing & Hachiko Statue
stops.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing is a Tokyo icon, and the loyal dog Hachiko's bronze statue nearby is one of the city's most beloved meeting points.
stops.transfer_note: Direct subway to Shibuya station.

stops.name: Pokemon Center, Nintendo Tokyo & Jump Shop
stops.description: Three must-visit stores for fans of Japanese gaming and anime culture, all located in or near the Shibuya-Shinjuku area with exclusive merchandise.
stops.transfer_note: Within or near Shibuya.

stops.name: Mega Don Quijote Shibuya
stops.description: A massive multi-floor discount store where you can spend hours browsing Japanese snacks, electronics, costumes, and quirky souvenirs at bargain prices.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Shibuya Crossing.

stops.name: Shibuya Yokocho
stops.description: A lively indoor alley of casual Japanese eateries and izakayas beneath the Scramble Square complex, great for trying a variety of regional dishes.
stops.transfer_note: Inside Shibuya Scramble Square, short walk from the crossing.

stops.name: Shibuya Sky
stops.description: An open-air rooftop observation deck atop Shibuya Scramble Square with 360-degree views and a dramatic view straight down onto the famous crossing.
stops.tip: Book tickets in advance online — slots sell out quickly.
stops.transfer_note: Inside Shibuya Scramble Square.

stops.name: 5 Crossties Coffee & A Happy Pancake
stops.description: Two of Shibuya's popular café stops — a specialty coffee shop and a restaurant known for its fluffy Japanese soufflé pancakes.
stops.transfer_note: Within Shibuya neighbourhood.

stops.name: Ueno
stops.description: A sprawling cultural district home to Tokyo's top museums, Ueno Zoo, Ueno Park, and Ameyoko market street — a great half-day base.
stops.transfer_note: Direct subway to Ueno station.

stops.name: Akihabara
stops.description: Tokyo's legendary Electric Town, packed with multi-floor arcades, anime and manga shops, retro gaming stores, and maid cafés.
stops.tip: Don't miss the multi-floor game centres for a classic Japanese arcade experience.
stops.transfer_note: Short subway ride or walk from Ueno.

stops.name: Asakusa
stops.description: Tokyo's most traditional neighbourhood, centred on Senso-ji temple, Nakamise shopping street, fortune-telling stalls, and classic Japanese street food.
stops.tip: Draw an omikuji fortune at Senso-ji for a quintessential Asakusa experience.
stops.transfer_note: Subway to Asakusa station.

stops.name: Wagyu beef restaurant, Asakusa
stops.description: A sit-down restaurant in Asakusa serving premium wagyu beef in lacquered bento-style boxes, a standout food experience in the area.
stops.transfer_note: Within Asakusa neighbourhood.

stops.name: Rainbow Bridge & Odaiba
stops.description: Tokyo's iconic suspension bridge over Tokyo Bay, best seen from the Odaiba waterfront at sunset for spectacular views of the city skyline.
stops.tip: Head to Odaiba waterfront in the late afternoon to catch the sunset.
stops.transfer_note: Yurikamome monorail or bus from central Tokyo to Odaiba.

stops.name: Hakone
stops.description: A scenic mountain resort town with hot springs, views of Mount Fuji, and the open-air museum, easily reached by Romancecar train from Shinjuku.
stops.transfer_note: Train from Shinjuku, roughly 90 minutes.

stops.name: Fuji Five Lakes
stops.description: The lake district at the base of Mount Fuji offering iconic reflections and close-up views of Japan's most famous peak.
stops.transfer_note: Bus or train from Shinjuku, roughly 2 hours.

stops.name: Yokohama
stops.description: Japan's second-largest city and a short ride from Tokyo, known for its vibrant Chinatown, scenic waterfront, and cosmopolitan atmosphere.
stops.transfer_note: Direct train from Shibuya or Shinjuku, roughly 30 minutes.

stops.name: Kawagoe
stops.description: Known as 'Little Edo', this preserved castle town features historic merchant warehouses, sweet potato snacks, and a famous bell tower.
stops.transfer_note: Direct train from Ikebukuro, roughly 30 minutes.

stops.name: Enoshima
stops.description: A small island connected to the coast by a causeway, featuring shrines, sea caves, and sweeping views of Sagami Bay and Mount Fuji.
stops.transfer_note: Train from Shinjuku via Odakyu line, roughly 70 minutes.

stops.name: Nikko
stops.description: A UNESCO World Heritage mountain town with lavishly decorated Tosho-gu shrine, waterfalls, and dramatic cedar forests.
stops.transfer_note: Tobu Nikko train from Asakusa, roughly 2 hours.

stops.name: Chichibu
stops.description: A lesser-known mountainous town west of Tokyo with atmospheric Shinto shrines, seasonal flower fields, and local whisky distilleries.
stops.transfer_note: Train from Ikebukuro via Seibu line, roughly 90 minutes.

stops.name: Mount Takao
stops.description: An accessible hiking mountain on the western edge of Tokyo with multiple trails and a summit view that stretches to Mount Fuji on clear days.
stops.transfer_note: Keio line direct from Shinjuku, roughly 50 minutes.

stops.name: Kamakura
stops.description: A historic coastal town south of Tokyo famous for its giant bronze Great Buddha, Zen temples, and hiking trails between shrines.
stops.transfer_note: JR Yokosuka line from Tokyo station, roughly 60 minutes.

routes.summary: Tokyo is one of the world's most electrifying cities, blending ancient shrines and neon-lit alleys with cutting-edge pop culture and world-class food. This five-day itinerary covers the city's most iconic neighbourhoods — Shinjuku, Shibuya, Akihabara, Ueno, and Asakusa — before pointing you toward standout day trips like Hakone, Kamakura, and the Fuji Five Lakes.

stops.name: Amsterdam Canal Ring
stops.description: The UNESCO-listed network of 17th-century canals lined with narrow gabled houses is Amsterdam's most iconic sight.

stops.name: Dutch Fries (Vlaamse Frites), Amsterdam
stops.description: Thick-cut twice-fried chips served with mayonnaise or satay sauce are a beloved Dutch street snack — commenters recommend Febo or any local snackbar.
stops.tip: Try a normal snackbar for authentic Dutch fries
stops.transfer_note: Short walk along the canals

stops.name: Vault Bar Amsterdam
stops.description: A moody cocktail bar serving inventive drinks in a dimly lit, atmospheric setting perfect for an evening out.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or tram from the canal area

stops.name: The Pool Bar Amsterdam
stops.description: A laid-back bar with multiple pool tables, making it a fun spot for a casual night out with drinks.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Vault Bar

stops.name: A'DAM Lookout
stops.description: A striking observation deck atop the A'DAM Tower in Amsterdam Noord offering 360-degree panoramic views over the city, plus a thrilling over-the-edge swing.
stops.transfer_note: Free ferry from Central Station to Amsterdam Noord

stops.name: Van Stapele Koekmakerij
stops.description: A tiny cult bakery famous for its single product — a warm, gooey chocolate cookie with a white chocolate centre that draws queues around the block.
stops.transfer_note: Ferry back to Central Station, then short walk

stops.name: Flying Dutchmen Cocktails
stops.description: An intimate, art-deco-inspired cocktail bar with a serious spirits library and skilled bartenders, ideal for a sophisticated nightcap.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Van Stapele

stops.name: Keukenhof Gardens
stops.description: One of the world's largest flower gardens, showcasing millions of tulips, daffodils and hyacinths across 32 hectares — a spectacular seasonal spectacle open mid-March to mid-May.
stops.tip: Book tickets online in advance — it sells out quickly
stops.transfer_note: Bus or coach from Amsterdam Centraal, roughly 30–40 minutes

routes.summary: Amsterdam enchants with its golden-age canal houses, world-class museums, and a vibrant food and nightlife scene that rewards curious visitors. This route covers the creator's top 10 picks — from iconic Dutch street food and craft cocktail bars to the panoramic A'DAM Lookout tower and a day-trip to the legendary Keukenhof tulip gardens outside the city.

stops.name: Burj Khalifa
stops.description: The world's tallest building offers breathtaking views from its observation decks high above the Dubai skyline.
stops.tip: Tickets are 179 AED — book online in advance to save.

stops.name: Dubai Mall
stops.description: One of the world's largest shopping and entertainment complexes, free to enter and explore.
stops.tip: Entry is free — great for exploring even without shopping.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Burj Khalifa

stops.name: Dubai Fountain
stops.description: The world's largest choreographed fountain show, set on the Burj Khalifa Lake with spectacular evening performances.
stops.tip: Free to watch — best enjoyed after dark from the waterfront promenade.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Dubai Mall

stops.name: Dubai Desert Safari
stops.description: A classic full-day or afternoon-into-evening experience combining dune bashing, sandboarding, camel rides, and a Bedouin camp dinner.
stops.tip: Packages range from 90–140 AED — shop around for the best deal.
stops.transfer_note: Car or organised tour pickup from hotel required

stops.name: Aquaventure Waterpark
stops.description: Atlantis's thrilling waterpark on Palm Jumeirah with record-breaking slides and a private beach.
stops.tip: Entry is 350 AED — arrive early to make the most of it.
stops.transfer_note: Car or taxi to Palm Jumeirah

stops.name: Jumeirah Beach
stops.description: A long stretch of public beach with stunning views of the Burj Al Arab, perfect for a free sunset visit.
stops.tip: Free entry — go at sunset for the best light and atmosphere.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Palm Jumeirah

stops.name: The Walk at JBR
stops.description: A lively beachfront promenade lined with shops, cafés, and street performers — free to stroll and enjoy.
stops.tip: Free to visit — great for an evening walk after the beach.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive or walk from Jumeirah Beach

stops.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
stops.description: One of the world's most magnificent mosques, with gleaming white marble, golden domes, and intricate inlaid floors — entry is free.
stops.tip: Free entry — consider a guided day tour for extra context.
stops.transfer_note: Car or organised day tour from Dubai, roughly 1.5 hours

stops.name: Heritage Village Abu Dhabi
stops.description: An open-air living museum recreating traditional Emirati life, crafts, and architecture along the Abu Dhabi Corniche.
stops.tip: Free to enter — combine with the mosque on the same day trip.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque

stops.name: Dubai Marina
stops.description: A stunning man-made canal city lined with skyscrapers, yacht berths, restaurants, and promenades — beautiful by day or night.

stops.name: Dubai Marina Boat Trip
stops.description: A scenic boat cruise through the marina waterways and out towards the Palm Jumeirah, offering brilliant skyline views at night.
stops.tip: Costs 99 AED — evening departures give the best views of the lit-up skyline.
stops.transfer_note: Departs from Dubai Marina

stops.name: Doors Dubai
stops.description: A popular rooftop bar and restaurant with skyline views and a buzzy atmosphere.

stops.name: Observatory Bar & Grill Dubai
stops.description: A high-altitude bar and grill with panoramic views over the marina.
stops.tip: Book/reserve ahead — this spot gets busy.

stops.name: Bussola Dubai
stops.description: A beloved Italian restaurant and bar on the water in Dubai Marina.

stops.name: Zouzou Dubai
stops.description: A trendy Middle Eastern-inspired restaurant with a lively crowd and great sharing plates.

stops.name: Asia Asia Dubai
stops.description: A visually spectacular pan-Asian restaurant suspended over Dubai Marina.

stops.name: Nobu Dubai
stops.description: The world-famous Japanese-Peruvian fusion restaurant with a Dubai outpost in Atlantis The Palm.

stops.name: Zuma Dubai
stops.description: An iconic modern Japanese izakaya restaurant in the DIFC, consistently one of Dubai's best tables.

stops.name: Pier 7 Dubai Marina
stops.description: A seven-storey tower in Dubai Marina with a different restaurant on each floor, all overlooking the water.
stops.tip: Best around sunset.

routes.summary: Dubai is a city of superlatives — the world's tallest tower, vast malls, golden desert dunes, and a glittering marina make it one of the most thrilling urban destinations on the planet. This 5-day route covers downtown landmarks, a desert safari, Palm Jumeirah, a day trip to Abu Dhabi, and a final evening on the water at Dubai Marina, with restaurant and gym recommendations woven throughout.

stops.name: Casa Batlló
stops.description: Gaudí's fantastical Passeig de Gràcia masterpiece, with its dragon-scale roof and bone-like façade, is one of the world's most extraordinary buildings.
stops.tip: Book tickets online in advance to skip the long queue outside.

stops.name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
stops.description: Gaudí's undulating stone apartment building on Passeig de Gràcia, famous for its warrior-like rooftop chimneys and free-flowing interior.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk along Passeig de Gràcia from Casa Batlló

stops.name: Casa Vicens
stops.description: Gaudí's first major work, covered in colourful Moorish-inspired tiles, sits in the Gràcia neighbourhood and is far less crowded than his later buildings.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or metro from Passeig de Gràcia to Gràcia neighbourhood

stops.name: Catedral de Barcelona
stops.description: The soaring Gothic cathedral at the heart of the Barri Gòtic, with a beautiful cloister housing white geese and free entry in the mornings.

stops.name: El Beso
stops.description: The famous sculpture 'The Kiss' is a romantic landmark and popular photo stop in the Gothic Quarter area.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from the Cathedral

stops.name: Plaça de Catalunya
stops.description: Barcelona's grand central square linking the old city to the Eixample, surrounded by fountains, pigeons, and major shopping streets.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from the Gothic Quarter

stops.name: Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria
stops.description: Barcelona's most famous covered market on Las Ramblas, packed with fresh produce, seafood, jamón, and colourful fruit stalls.
stops.transfer_note: Located on Las Ramblas, a short walk from Plaça de Catalunya

stops.name: El Nacional Barcelona
stops.description: A stunning 1940s-style food hall on Passeig de Gràcia housing multiple restaurants and bars under one spectacular roof.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Las Ramblas to Passeig de Gràcia

stops.name: Park Güell
stops.description: Gaudí's colourful hilltop park offers mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona.
stops.tip: Book the monumental zone ticket in advance — it sells out fast.
stops.transfer_note: Metro or bus to the Gràcia/Park Güell area

stops.name: Sagrada Família
stops.description: Gaudí's unfinished basilica is Barcelona's most iconic landmark, with breathtaking stained-glass interiors and towering spires still under construction.
stops.tip: Buy tickets online months ahead — timed entry is mandatory.
stops.transfer_note: Metro to Sagrada Família stop

stops.name: Barceloneta Beach
stops.description: Barcelona's most central urban beach is perfect for a final-day swim, sunbathe, and seafood lunch by the Mediterranean.
stops.transfer_note: Metro to Barceloneta or a walk down Las Ramblas to the sea

routes.summary: Barcelona is one of Europe's most vibrant cities, blending world-class Modernista architecture with a buzzing food scene and a lively street culture. This 5-day itinerary works through Gaudí's iconic buildings on day one, dives into the Gothic Quarter and Las Ramblas on day two, and — based on what the video reveals — likely covers Park Güell, the Sagrada Família, and the city's beaches across the remaining days.

stops.name: Colosseum
stops.description: The world's most iconic ancient amphitheatre, seating up to 80,000 spectators in its Roman heyday.
stops.tip: Book tickets in advance; arena floor access costs €24+.

stops.name: Roman Forum
stops.description: The heart of ancient Roman public life, packed with temples, arches, and sacred ruins.
stops.tip: Included in Colosseum ticket — don't skip it.
stops.transfer_note: 2-minute walk from the Colosseum

stops.name: Palatine Hill
stops.description: The legendary founding hill of Rome offering sweeping views over the Forum below.
stops.tip: Also included in Colosseum ticket.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from the Roman Forum

stops.name: Altare della Patria
stops.description: Rome's grand neoclassical monument to unified Italy, free to enter with a paid panoramic lift to the top.
stops.tip: Lift to the roof terrace costs €15 for the best city views.
stops.transfer_note: About 12-minute walk from Palatine Hill

stops.name: Church of Sant'Ignazio di Loyola
stops.description: A free Baroque church hiding one of Rome's most jaw-dropping trompe-l'œil ceiling frescoes.
stops.tip: Free entry — look straight up at the illusionistic dome fresco.
stops.transfer_note: About 8-minute walk from Altare della Patria

stops.name: Piazza Navona
stops.description: Rome's most theatrical Baroque square, anchored by Bernini's spectacular Fountain of the Four Rivers.
stops.tip: Arrive early morning to enjoy it without the crowds.

stops.name: The Pantheon
stops.description: A breathtakingly preserved Roman temple turned church with a 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome.
stops.tip: Entry is €5 — book ahead to avoid queues.
stops.transfer_note: 5-minute walk from Piazza Navona

stops.name: Trevi Fountain
stops.description: Rome's most famous Baroque fountain where tradition says a thrown coin guarantees your return.
stops.tip: Go after 9 pm — entry is now ticketed during the day.
stops.transfer_note: About 8-minute walk from the Pantheon

stops.name: Spanish Steps
stops.description: Rome's grandest staircase of 135 steps linking Piazza di Spagna to the hilltop church of Trinità dei Monti.
stops.tip: Free to visit; avoid sitting on the steps to dodge fines.
stops.transfer_note: About 10-minute walk from Trevi Fountain

stops.name: Villa Borghese Gardens
stops.description: Rome's most beloved park, perfect for a golden-hour stroll with sweeping views over the city's rooftops.
stops.tip: Head to the Pincio terrace viewpoint for the best sunset panorama.
stops.transfer_note: About 15-minute walk from the Spanish Steps

stops.name: Vatican Museums
stops.description: One of the world's great art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling.
stops.tip: Book skip-the-line tickets online; guided entry is €25+.

stops.name: Saint Peter's Basilica
stops.description: The world's largest church and the spiritual heart of Catholicism, with Michelangelo's Pietà inside and a climbable dome offering panoramic views.
stops.tip: Dome climb costs €10 — stairs are free, lift is faster.
stops.transfer_note: 10-minute walk from the Vatican Museums

stops.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
stops.description: A Roman mausoleum turned papal fortress turned museum, with incredible views of the Tiber from its ramparts.
stops.tip: Entry is €13; the rooftop terrace view of St Peter's is superb.
stops.transfer_note: 1-minute walk from Saint Peter's Basilica

stops.name: Janiculum Hill
stops.description: Rome's best panoramic viewpoint offers a sweeping 180-degree sunset vista across the entire city skyline.
stops.tip: Free entry — arrive just before sunset for the best light.
stops.transfer_note: About 15-minute walk from Castel Sant'Angelo

stops.name: Dinner in Trastevere
stops.description: Rome's most atmospheric neighbourhood for an evening meal, packed with cobblestone lanes, ivy-clad trattorias, and a buzzing local crowd.
stops.tip: Creator didn't specify — choose one you like in the area.
stops.transfer_note: About 15-minute walk from Janiculum Hill

routes.summary: Rome is one of the world's great open-air museums, where ancient ruins, Renaissance masterpieces, and Baroque fountains sit side by side on walkable streets. This itinerary covers the city entirely on foot over three days, hitting the Colosseum complex and hidden churches on day one, the iconic piazzas and fountains on day two, and the Vatican with a Trastevere dinner to close things out.

stops.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
stops.description: Sacred jungle sanctuary where hundreds of long-tailed macaques roam freely among ancient temple ruins.

stops.name: Tirta Empul Temple
stops.description: Revered Hindu water temple where visitors can partake in a traditional purification ritual in holy spring pools.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Ubud centre

stops.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
stops.description: One of Bali's most accessible and photogenic waterfalls, surrounded by lush tropical greenery.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Tirta Empul

stops.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
stops.description: Iconic stepped rice paddies carved into a hillside just north of Ubud, offering sweeping jungle views.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Ubud centre

stops.name: Bali Swing, Ubud
stops.description: Thrilling jungle swing that arcs you out over lush rice terraces and palm-filled valleys.

stops.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
stops.description: Pre-dawn hike up an active volcano rewarded with breathtaking sunrise views over the caldera lake.
stops.transfer_note: Early morning drive required from Ubud

stops.name: ATV Ride Experience, Ubud
stops.description: Off-road quad biking through rice fields, jungle tracks, and traditional villages around Ubud.

stops.name: White Water Rafting, Ayung River
stops.description: Scenic whitewater rafting through lush jungle gorges on Bali's most popular rafting river.

stops.name: Angel's Billabong, Nusa Penida
stops.description: Natural infinity rock pool on the island's rugged west coast with crystal-clear turquoise water.
stops.transfer_note: Boat transfer from Sanur or Padang Bai, then scooter or car on the island

stops.name: Broken Beach, Nusa Penida
stops.description: Stunning natural archway carved into clifftop rock forming a circular cove with vivid blue water.
stops.transfer_note: Short ride from Angel's Billabong

stops.name: Kelingking Beach, Nusa Penida
stops.description: Nusa Penida's most iconic viewpoint, with a T-Rex-shaped cliff plunging down to a pristine white-sand beach.
stops.transfer_note: Car or scooter ride across the island

stops.name: Crystal Bay, Nusa Penida
stops.description: Calm, sheltered bay perfect for snorkelling with manta rays and enjoying a peaceful beach sunset.
stops.transfer_note: Short ride from Kelingking

stops.name: Seminyak Beach
stops.description: Bali's most stylish beach strip, great for surfing in the morning and watching stunning sunsets in the evening.
stops.transfer_note: Drive from Ubud or Nusa Penida ferry port

stops.name: Potato Head Beach Club
stops.description: Bali's most iconic beach club with a famous circular wall, pools, and all-day dining on the Seminyak shore.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or drive along Seminyak Beach

stops.name: Seminyak Square
stops.description: Open-air shopping and dining hub in the heart of Seminyak with boutiques and restaurants.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from the beach

stops.name: Seminyak Village
stops.description: Stylish modern shopping mall with a distinctive curved wooden roof, anchoring Seminyak's retail scene.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Seminyak Square

stops.name: Cafe Bali
stops.description: Highly recommended local café
stops.tip: Creator highly recommends this spot for a food trip.

stops.name: Garuda Wisnu Kencana Cultural Park
stops.description: Dramatic cultural park dominated by a towering statue of the god Wisnu riding the mythical Garuda bird.
stops.transfer_note: Drive from Seminyak

stops.name: Uluwatu Temple
stops.description: Ancient clifftop sea temple perched 70 metres above the Indian Ocean with sweeping sunset views.
stops.transfer_note: Drive south along the Bukit Peninsula

stops.name: Kecak Dance at Uluwatu Temple
stops.description: Mesmerising traditional Balinese fire and kecak dance performance held at Uluwatu Temple at sunset.
stops.transfer_note: At Uluwatu Temple

stops.name: Padang-Padang Beach
stops.description: Small, sheltered beach accessed through a cave, famous for great surf and the film Eat Pray Love.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Uluwatu Temple

stops.name: Tanah Barak
stops.description: Scenic clifftop viewpoint or landmark in the Uluwatu area offering coastal panoramas.

stops.name: The Edge Beach Club, Uluwatu
stops.description: Clifftop infinity pool beach club with dramatic ocean views over the Indian Ocean.

stops.name: Palmilla Beach Club, Uluwatu
stops.description: Relaxed beachside club on the Bukit Peninsula with a natural pool setting and tropical vibes.

stops.name: Sundays Beach Club, Uluwatu
stops.description: Hidden beach club at the base of a cliff accessible by funicular, set on a pristine private beach.

stops.name: Single Fin Beach Club, Uluwatu
stops.description: Iconic clifftop bar and restaurant overlooking Uluwatu's famous surf break, best visited on Sundays.

stops.name: Minoo, Uluwatu
stops.description: Stylish beach club and dining spot in the Uluwatu area recommended for its setting and atmosphere.

routes.summary: Bali is one of Southeast Asia's most iconic destinations, blending lush jungle temples, terraced rice paddies, dramatic clifftop beaches, and a vibrant surf culture into one island. This 6-day route moves through Ubud's spiritual heart, a full-day island escape to Nusa Penida, a laid-back beach day in Seminyak, and two days exploring the clifftop wonders of Uluwatu.

stops.name: Palma de Mallorca Airport
stops.description: Fly in and pick up your rental car — essential for exploring the island at your own pace.
stops.tip: Pick up your car rental at the airport on arrival.

stops.name: Palma Cathedral (La Seu)
stops.description: One of Europe's great Gothic cathedrals, with spectacular rose windows and an interior designed partly by Gaudí.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from the airport into Palma city centre.

stops.name: Restaurant Illeta
stops.description: A stunning restaurant built on a rocky islet connected by a footbridge, offering seafood with jaw-dropping turquoise water views.
stops.tip: Book ahead — this iconic spot fills up fast in summer.
stops.transfer_note: Drive west from Palma towards Camp de Mar area.

stops.name: Beach Club Gran Folies
stops.description: A relaxed cliff-terrace beach club with sun loungers and cocktails, perfect for sunbathing and swimming until sunset.
stops.tip: Arrive for golden hour to catch the best sunset views.

stops.name: Valldemossa
stops.description: A fairy-tale hilltop village of honey-coloured stone, cobbled lanes, and flower-filled balconies set in the Tramuntana mountains.
stops.tip: Arrive early to explore the lanes before the crowds arrive.
stops.transfer_note: Drive north from Palma into the Serra de Tramuntana, roughly 30 minutes.

stops.name: Aromas
stops.description: A charming café in Valldemossa famous for its local speciality — a potato bun filled with ice cream, best enjoyed in the garden terrace.
stops.tip: Order the potato bun with ice cream — a Mallorcan must-try.
stops.transfer_note: Located within Valldemossa village, short walk from the main square.

stops.name: Deia
stops.description: A breathtakingly pretty village of terracotta rooftops and lush gardens tumbling down to the sea, beloved by artists and writers.
stops.tip: Drive 10 minutes from Valldemossa — another adorable village.
stops.transfer_note: Short 10-minute drive along the mountain road from Valldemossa.

stops.name: Can Costa
stops.description: A charming garden restaurant with red parasols and bougainvillea, serving traditional Mallorcan cuisine just outside the village.
stops.tip: Just outside Valldemossa — great for a leisurely lunch stop.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive just outside Valldemossa village.

stops.name: Soller
stops.description: A picturesque market town in the Tramuntana valley, famous for its vintage tram running through the main square past a striking stone church.
stops.tip: Ride the vintage tram from Sóller down to Port de Sóller.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive north from Deià along the mountain road.

stops.name: Calo del Moro
stops.description: One of Mallorca's most photographed secret coves, with crystal-clear turquoise water enclosed by dramatic limestone cliffs.
stops.tip: Arrive very early — the small car park fills up quickly.
stops.transfer_note: Drive southeast from Palma, car recommended.

stops.name: S'Almonia
stops.description: A wild and unspoilt rocky cove near the island's southern tip, ideal for snorkelling in gin-clear water.
stops.tip: All these beaches are close to each other — easy to combine.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Calo del Moro along the coast.

stops.name: Cala Llombards
stops.description: A sheltered sandy bay framed by red and golden cliffs, with calm shallow water perfect for swimming.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from S'Almonia.

stops.name: Platja de Santanyi
stops.description: A wide sandy beach near the pretty town of Santanyí, with beach bars and a relaxed holiday atmosphere.
stops.transfer_note: Short drive from Cala Llombards.

stops.name: Southeast coast calas
stops.description: Continue exploring the cluster of stunning southeast coves — all close together and best visited by car for a full day of swimming and sunbathing.
stops.tip: Dedicate the full day to beach hopping — the calas are very close.

days.label: West Coast — Ca's Patró March & Sunset

stops.name: Ca's Patró March
stops.description: A legendary waterside restaurant perched right on the rocks of a turquoise cove, serving fresh seafood with one of Mallorca's most spectacular views.
stops.tip: Queue for when they open at 12pm — it gets fully booked very fast.
stops.transfer_note: Drive to the west coast, car essential — the restaurant is accessed via a narrow coastal road.

stops.name: Cala Sant Vicenc Hotel
stops.description: A modern beachfront resort with terraced pools stepping down to the sea, offering a dramatic mountain and cove backdrop.
stops.transfer_note: Located on the northwest coast near Cala Sant Vicenç.

routes.summary: Mallorca is one of the Mediterranean's most rewarding islands, blending turquoise coves, dramatic mountain villages, and a vibrant food scene into a single destination. This five-day itinerary covers the historic capital Palma, the enchanting Serra de Tramuntana villages, two full days of beach-hopping along the southeast coast, and a final day on the west coast — all best explored by rental car.

stops.name: Alti Suites Santorini
stops.description: A hidden-gem caldera-view suite hotel with private plunge pools and stunning sunset vistas over the Aegean.
stops.tip: Creator calls it a hidden gem — book early as it's small.
stops.transfer_note: Short taxi or ATV ride from Santorini airport

stops.name: ATV or car rental, Santorini
stops.description: Renting an ATV or car is the creator's recommended way to explore the island freely at your own pace.
stops.tip: Rent an ATV or car — best way to get around the island.
stops.transfer_note: Available near most towns and at the port

stops.name: Oia, Santorini
stops.description: The most iconic and photogenic village in Santorini, famous for its blue-domed churches, cave houses, and breathtaking caldera views.
stops.tip: Go early morning to beat the crowds for photos.
stops.transfer_note: Short ATV or car ride north from Imerovigli

stops.name: Karma Restaurant Santorini
stops.description: A tucked-away local restaurant beloved for its relaxed vibe, resident cats, and hearty Greek dishes like chickpea soup.
stops.tip: Tucked away and they have cats — a charming hidden spot.

stops.name: Barolo Restaurant Santorini
stops.description: An elegant dinner option serving refined Mediterranean dishes in a sophisticated evening setting.

stops.name: Santorini Catamaran Cruise
stops.description: A sailing cruise around the volcanic caldera, offering swimming stops, stunning views of the cliffs, and a way to avoid the onshore crowds.
stops.tip: Book a morning departure if you want to avoid the crowds.
stops.transfer_note: Departs from Vlychada or Ammoudi Bay port

stops.name: Caldera viewpoint, Imerovigli
stops.description: Soak in the sweeping caldera panorama from the terrace of your hotel on your last morning before departing.
stops.transfer_note: At your hotel

routes.summary: Santorini is one of the world's most iconic island destinations, famous for its whitewashed clifftop villages, volcanic caldera views, and spectacular sunsets. This 4-day itinerary covers a hidden-gem hotel base, the postcard-perfect village of Oia, local dining spots tucked away from the crowds, and a catamaran cruise around the caldera.

stops.name: Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport
stops.description: Main international gateway to Paris, served by the RER B line directly into the city.
stops.tip: Take the RER B line to Gare du Nord to reach central Paris.

stops.name: Champs-Élysées
stops.description: Paris's most famous boulevard lined with luxury boutiques, cafés, and the Louis Vuitton flagship store.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or metro from Gare du Nord

stops.name: Arc de Triomphe
stops.description: Napoleon's monumental triumphal arch standing at the top of the Champs-Élysées, with sweeping city views from the top.
stops.transfer_note: At the top of the Champs-Élysées

stops.name: Carette
stops.description: Elegant Parisian salon de thé in the 16th arrondissement, beloved for its pastries and brunch near the Trocadéro.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from the Arc de Triomphe

stops.name: Trocadéro
stops.description: Iconic esplanade offering the most celebrated panoramic view of the Eiffel Tower across the Seine.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Carette

stops.name: Eiffel Tower
stops.description: Paris's defining iron landmark, best experienced by going up for sweeping city views and staying for the nightly light show.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Trocadéro

stops.name: Seine River Cruise
stops.description: Scenic boat cruise along the Seine passing Paris's most famous monuments illuminated at night.
stops.transfer_note: Depart from near the Eiffel Tower

stops.name: Bouillon Pigalle
stops.description: Lively and affordable classic French brasserie in the Pigalle neighbourhood, famous for its long queues and great value.
stops.transfer_note: Metro from the Eiffel Tower area to Pigalle

stops.name: Nearby bakery breakfast, Paris
stops.description: A classic Parisian start to the day with fresh croissants and coffee at a local boulangerie.
stops.tip: No specific place — pick any similar option nearby.

stops.name: Louvre Museum
stops.description: The world's largest art museum, home to the Mona Lisa and thousands of masterpieces housed in a stunning glass pyramid complex.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or metro from hotel

stops.name: Jardin des Tuileries
stops.description: Beautiful formal garden stretching between the Louvre and Place de la Concorde, perfect for a leisurely stroll.
stops.transfer_note: Direct walk from the Louvre

stops.name: Place de la Concorde
stops.description: Paris's largest public square featuring the ancient Egyptian Luxor Obelisk at its centre.
stops.transfer_note: At the end of the Tuileries garden

stops.name: Place Vendôme
stops.description: Prestigious octagonal square in the 1st arrondissement surrounded by luxury jewellers and the historic Ritz Paris.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Place de la Concorde

stops.name: Palais Garnier
stops.description: Paris's opulent 19th-century opera house with a jaw-dropping interior featuring Chagall's painted ceiling and gilded auditorium.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Place Vendôme

stops.name: Galeries Lafayette Paris Haussmann
stops.description: Iconic Parisian department store with a stunning art nouveau glass dome, a Jellycat patisserie pop-up, and a rooftop with Eiffel Tower views.
stops.tip: Watch the sunset from the free rooftop terrace.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Palais Garnier

stops.name: Zapi
stops.description: Trendy Paris restaurant for dinner, visited on the creator's Day Two itinerary.

stops.name: Disneyland Paris
stops.description: Europe's most-visited theme park resort featuring two parks, fairytale castle, daily parades, and spectacular nightly fireworks over Sleeping Beauty Castle.
stops.tip: Take the RER A line to Marne-la-Vallée station; get the RER A back to Paris in the evening.
stops.transfer_note: RER A line from central Paris to Marne-la-Vallée, about 40 minutes

days.label: Île de la Cité, Left Bank & Montmartre

stops.name: Maison Louvard
stops.description: Charming Parisian café and bakery, a favourite for breakfast before a day of sightseeing.

stops.name: Place Louis Aragon
stops.description: Picturesque square on the Île Saint-Louis used as a filming location in 'The Summer I Turned Pretty'.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or metro to Île de la Cité area

stops.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
stops.description: Paris's breathtaking Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, recently reopened after years of post-fire restoration.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Place Louis Aragon

stops.name: Relais de l'Entrecôte
stops.description: Legendary no-menu Parisian steak-frites institution where the only choice is how you'd like your entrecôte cooked.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk or metro from Notre-Dame

stops.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
stops.description: Elegant 17th-century formal garden on the Left Bank, perfect for a post-lunch stroll past fountains and manicured lawns.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Relais de l'Entrecôte

stops.name: Montmartre
stops.description: Paris's bohemian hilltop village neighbourhood filled with artists, charming cobbled streets, and sweeping city views.
stops.transfer_note: Metro from Luxembourg area to Montmartre

stops.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
stops.description: Gleaming white Romano-Byzantine basilica crowning the Montmartre hill with panoramic views over all of Paris.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk up the hill in Montmartre

stops.name: La Maison Rose
stops.description: Iconic pale pink restaurant facade on a cobbled Montmartre corner, one of the most photographed spots in Paris.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from Sacré-Cœur

stops.name: Rue de l'Abreuvoir
stops.description: One of Montmartre's most charming and photogenic cobblestone streets, lined with ivy-covered buildings.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk from La Maison Rose

stops.name: Wall of Love (Le Mur des Je t'aime)
stops.description: A public artwork in Square Jehan Rictus featuring 'I love you' written in 250 languages on a mosaic of blue tiles.
stops.transfer_note: Short walk within Montmartre

routes.summary: Paris is one of the world's most romantic and culturally rich cities, famous for its iconic landmarks, world-class museums, and legendary food scene. This four-day itinerary covers the classic highlights — from the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre to a full day at Disneyland Paris — finishing with the bohemian streets of Montmartre and the Left Bank.
